samples.summary: Browser login page has no handling for the new 401 the callback can now return
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27 is the only browser entry point into the OAuth flow (`to={`${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/github`}`). Before this change `GET /auth/github/callback` could not fail for a normal user; it now throws `UnauthorizedException('Login session expired or invalid...')` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:183 / :210) whenever the `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie is absent or stale. That cookie has `maxAge: 5 * 60 * 1000` (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:161), so a user who sits on GitHub's consent screen for more than five minutes — or who has cookies blocked for the backend origin, or who completes an in-flight login across a deploy — lands on a raw Nest JSON 401 page on the *backend* origin with no link back to the app. The frontend consumer was not updated to catch or recover from this new failure mode (no error route, no retry affordance). The fix likely belongs on the backend: redirect to `FRONTEND_URL` with an error query parameter instead of throwing, or on the frontend by adding a callback-error landing page.
searchedFor: Grep for a callback/error route in packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: Every already-installed CLI version breaks against an upgraded backend (mode=cli now 400s without nonce/code_challenge)
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:107-119 throws `BadRequestException` for any `?mode=cli&port=` request that does not also carry `nonce` and `code_challenge`. The only in-repo client (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:55-58) was updated, but published `@wafflebase/cli` versions send exactly `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` (the pre-change form still recorded at docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md:473). Any deployed CLI, CI script or container image pinned to an older version stops being able to run `wafflebase login` the moment the backend ships — with no server-side grace period. This is documented as deliberate in docs/design/cli.md:246-256, so this is a heads-up on the out-of-repo blast radius (release notes / version pin) rather than a claim the logic is wrong.

samples.summary: backend.md still documents the pre-change /auth/github and /auth/cli/exchange contracts
samples.evidence: docs/design/backend.md:103-115 says `GET /auth/github` uses guard `AuthGuard('github')` and that the callback simply upserts the user and sets cookies — no mention of `GitHubAuthGuard`, the `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie, the `w.`-prefixed browser state, or the fact that the callback now rejects a missing/mismatched `state`. docs/design/backend.md:144-147 documents the exchange body as `{ code }`, but packages/backend/src/auth/auth.dto.ts now accepts (and packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts:120 now requires, for challenged codes) `codeVerifier`. rest-api.md and cli.md were updated; backend.md was not. The backticked-path CI check does not verify prose accuracy.

samples.summary: packages/backend/README.md auth-flow walkthrough describes the pre-state-binding flow
samples.evidence: packages/backend/README.md:389-399 enumerates the OAuth flow with no `state`/cookie step, and packages/backend/README.md:184-185 describes `GET /auth/github` as simply 'Initiate GitHub OAuth flow'. Both now omit the mandatory `wafflebase_oauth_state` double submit added in packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:147-163 and enforced at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:174-213. Nothing mechanically checks these files.

samples.summary: Agent-facing skill files still show the error envelope without the new `command` field
samples.evidence: packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:57 documents the stderr envelope as `{ "error": { "code": "CONFIRMATION_REQ", "message": ... } }` and packages/cli/skills/docs-read-content.md:86 as `{ "error": { "code": "TYPE_MISMATCH", ... } }`. Both paths now emit through `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope` (packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:146, packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202) which adds `command` and drops the pretty-printing. packages/cli/README.md:117 and docs/design/cli.md were updated; the skill files, which are what agents read as the contract, were not.

samples.summary: Two new login tests omit WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG, so `announceLoginUrl` writes into the developer's real ~/.wafflebase
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:123 sets `process.env.WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG = configPath`, but the two later tests (line 208 and line 287) set only `WAFFLEBASE_SESSION`. Under vitest stderr is not a TTY, so `announceLoginUrl` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:210) resolves `join(dirname(getConfigPath()), 'login-url.txt')` against the real config location and does `mkdirSync` + `writeFileSync` there. The suite's `afterEach` only removes the tmp `urlPath`, so the real directory is created (and briefly holds a login URL) as a side effect of running tests. Confirming needs a run with `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG` unset to see the real home path used.

verdict.reason: Verified the absence directly. The callback now throws UnauthorizedException on a missing/stale state cookie (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:183, :210, reached from :120) and nothing converts that into a user-recoverable response: the backend has no exception filter (no matches for ExceptionFilter/@Catch/useGlobalFilters/APP_FILTER under packages/backend/src) and main.ts:30-79 registers only parsers/pipe/CORS; the only res.redirect calls are the two success paths (auth.controller.ts:145, :154). The state cookie is 5-minute-lived (github-auth.guard.ts:24 applied at :161) and is cleared unconditionally on the failing callback (auth.controller.ts:221-228), so the flow dead-ends on a raw Nest JSON 401 on the backend origin. On the consumer side the browser entry is a bare off-origin navigation (packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:26-29); the login page has no error awareness (packages/frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx:14-80) and App.tsx:79-131 declares no callback/error route. A wide grep for searchParams/error=/authError across packages/frontend/src surfaced only unrelated notification and folder params, and there is no proxy/edge config that could rewrite the response. This is a changed endpoint contract with an unupdated consumer on a reachable path — in lane and blocking at major.

finding.summary: Every already-installed CLI version breaks against an upgraded backend (mode=cli now 400s without nonce/code_challenge)
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:107-119 throws `BadRequestException` for any `?mode=cli&port=` request that does not also carry `nonce` and `code_challenge`. The only in-repo client (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:55-58) was updated, but published `@wafflebase/cli` versions send exactly `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` (the pre-change form still recorded at docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md:473). Any deployed CLI, CI script or container image pinned to an older version stops being able to run `wafflebase login` the moment the backend ships — with no server-side grace period. verdict.reason: The guard code exists as quoted (github-auth.guard.ts:98-119 throws BadRequestException for mode=cli without a bounded nonce/code_challenge), but it is not a blocking blast-radius defect. I grepped every producer of a `mode=cli` start URL in the repo: the sole one is packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:56-58, which supplies both parameters (minted at login.ts:47-51); the browser flow at packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27 sends no `mode` and takes the unaffected `w.` branch at guard:132-134; the remaining hits are specs that pass both parameters (github-auth.guard.spec.ts:75-180, login-callback.test.ts:169). No in-repo caller is left broken or bypassing. The only affected consumer is a previously-published CLI outside this repo, and that break is the explicitly recorded design decision (docs/design/cli.md:246-256; docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:55-61; guard doc comment lines 68-86), with the mirror-image old-backend message already shipped in the CLI at login.ts:388-392. Whether a grace period should have been offered instead of a hard cutover is the security-design trade-off this lens defers on; nothing bypasses the guard. The reviewer themselves frames it as a release-notes heads-up rather than a claim the logic is wrong.
